documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

53F office manager, transferring care after her prior primary care doctor retired. Wants one office she can actually reach. No acute concerns today.

PMH
- COPD. Dx'd at prior practice, she isn't sure what year. Gets winded on 2 flights of stairs, walks fine on flat ground. Uses albuterol maybe 2-3x/week, more in cold weather. On tiotropium daily, uses it most days. No hospitalizations or prednisone bursts she can recall. Never had breathing tests explained to her.
- HTN on amlodipine 5 for years. Doesn't check at home.
- Genital warts in her 20s-30s, several excisions and cryo treatments through the 2000s. None since.

PSH: lap chole 2010. Wart excisions/cryo as above.

Meds: albuterol HFA 2 puffs q4-6h prn; tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

FHx: mother - cervical cancer at 42, deceased. Father - lung cancer at 58, deceased. Sister - CIN II.

Social: office manager. Smokes about a pack a day, started at 25, so roughly 29 pack-years. Has tried cutting down on her own, not interested in a quit date right now. Wine 1-2 glasses a week. No drugs.

ROS: chronic exertional dyspnea as above, no chest pain, no hemoptysis, no weight change, no GI or GU complaints. Postmenopausal.

Exam: BP above goal on repeat, otherwise vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing, faint smoker's voice. HEENT unremarkable. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs: mildly prolonged expiration, no wheeze or crackles. Abd soft, well-healed lap scars. Ext no edema, no clubbing. Skin no concerning lesions seen.

A/P
1. COPD - no spirometry on file that she knows of. Will get office spirometry next month once records are in. Continue tiotropium + albuterol. Inhaler technique reviewed, good.
2. Tobacco - discussed briefly, she knows. Not ready. Will keep asking.
3. HTN - a little high today, she was rushing in. Recheck at the COPD visit. Continue amlodipine 5.
4. Lung cancer screening - qualifies (age, ~29 pk-yr, current). Will order after spirometry visit.
5. Health maintenance - records requested. CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, one-time HCV and HIV today. Flu shot given. Will ask records about colonoscopy, Pap, mammogram, vaccines.

RTC ~4 weeks.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Evelyn,

All of your bloodwork from Tuesday came back fine: kidney and liver tests normal, blood counts normal, cholesterol in a reasonable range, and the A1c shows no sign of diabetes. The hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative, so those are one-and-done.

See you next month for the breathing test.

Primary care

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records received from prior primary care office (closed practice), 38 pages, scanned.

Summary abstracted by MA:
- Problem list: COPD; hypertension; tobacco use; history of condyloma acuminatum, treated.
- Medications: albuterol HFA prn, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily. No allergies listed.
- Colonoscopy 2018: normal, repeat 10 years.
- Cervical cytology with HPV co-test 2019: negative.
- Screening mammogram 2020: negative, BI-RADS 1.
- Immunizations: Tdap 05/2016. COVID-19 Pfizer 03/19/2021 and 04/09/2021 (copy of card).
- No spirometry report in the packet.

Forwarded to PCP for review.

reports.text:
Office spirometry, pre- and post-bronchodilator (albuterol 4 puffs via spacer). Acceptable and repeatable efforts.
Post-bronchodilator: FEV1 1.62 L (66% predicted). FVC 2.57 L (83% predicted). FEV1/FVC 0.63.
No significant bronchodilator response.
reports.conclusion: Moderate obstructive ventilatory defect (GOLD 2), without significant bronchodilator response.

documents.title: COPD Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for spirometry and BP recheck. Breathing same as always. Albuterol a couple times a week. No cough change, no sputum change, no ER visits. Still smoking ~1 ppd.

Records from prior PCP reviewed: colonoscopy 2018 normal, Pap/HPV 2019 negative, mammo 2020 negative. No PFTs in the packet.

O: BP improved, see flowsheet. Lungs: prolonged expiration, no wheeze. Heart RRR.
Spirometry (see report): post-BD FEV1 1.62 L, 66% pred; FEV1/FVC 0.63; no significant BD response.

A/P
- COPD, moderate obstruction (GOLD 2). Few symptoms, no exacerbations. Tiotropium alone is reasonable. Continue albuterol prn.
- HTN: better today. Continue amlodipine 5.
- Tobacco: we talked about the spirometry result as a reason. She listened, not ready to set a date.
- PCV20 today.
- LDCT lung screening ordered. Screening mammogram ordered (due Nov).
- Colonoscopy next due 2028.

f/u 6 months, sooner prn.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
INDICATION: Lung cancer screening. Current smoker, approximately 29 pack-years. Baseline study.
TECHNIQUE: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or pleural effusion. Central airways patent. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Heart size normal. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months.

reports.text:
Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison is made to the outside study from 2020.
The breasts are scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1: negative. Routine screening mammogram in 1 year.

documents.title: Imaging results
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Evelyn, both of your screening tests came back normal. The lung CT showed no nodules and the mammogram was negative. Each one gets repeated in a year and we'll send reminders. -Nursing

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT

Doing well. Busy season at work. Breathing stable through the winter, no flares, albuterol a few times a week. Tiotropium daily. Amlodipine daily. Smoking still about a pack a day. Mood fine.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, BP fine today. Pleasant, in no distress. HEENT normal, no nodes. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs with prolonged expiration, no wheeze, no crackles. Breasts deferred to mammography per her preference. Abdomen soft, nontender. Ext no edema. Skin without suspicious lesions.

Screens: PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

Health maintenance:
- Colonoscopy 2018 normal, next 2028.
- Cervical: co-test 2019 negative, next due 2024.
- Mammogram 11/2021 neg, next Nov.
- LDCT 11/2021 Lung-RADS 1, next Nov.
- Vaccines: Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months. PCV20 done. Tdap 2016. COVID boosted Dec.

A/P
1. COPD GOLD 2, stable on tiotropium + prn albuterol.
2. HTN controlled on amlodipine 5.
3. Tobacco: advised to quit; offered help whenever she wants it. Declines for now.
4. Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids.

RTC 6 months, Shingrix #2 nurse visit.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Evelyn - labs from Wednesday all look good. Nothing to change. Remember to book the second shingles shot in the next few months.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Shingrix dose 2 of 2, 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Screening questions reviewed, no contraindications. Had a sore arm and was tired for a day after dose 1, nothing else. Tolerated today without issue. Series complete.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u BP and COPD.

No changes since spring. Summer was easy on her lungs. No exacerbations, no antibiotics or steroids anywhere this year. Using albuterol 1-2x/wk. Tiotropium daily. Taking amlodipine. Still ~1 ppd; she says work stress makes it the wrong time.

Exam: BP at goal. Lungs prolonged expiration, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P: COPD stable, HTN controlled. Brief cessation advice again. Flu shot today. LDCT and mammogram due in Nov, reminders sent. RTC March for physical.
